title: Delegate
markdown:
**What it is:** The place where you decide what the Executive may do without asking you. **Delegate** is in the main menu, one page in three tabs along the top: **As you**, **As me** and **Approvals**. Each tab shows where it stands, for example **Your inbox**, **On** and **Balanced**, so you can read all three without opening them. A link to one of them opens that tab. **What it does for you** opens beside the page from its button.

**What it does:**

- The Executive can work for you two ways. **As you**: in your name, from your own mailbox, so it looks like you did it. **As me**: in its own name, from its own accounts, so people can see your Executive did it.
- **Approvals** holds the one Approvals level, which decides for both what goes on its own and what comes to you as an Approve card. It is the same level on every channel: the app, email and every chat app.
- **In training**, on either side, sits above Approvals: while it is on, nothing goes out on its own, on any level. Each thing waits on a card that says what it would have done. Approve it, tick **on its own next time**, and from then on that goes on its own where Approvals lets it.
- **What it does for you** says what the Executive does with your settings right now. It only reads. Nothing on it changes a setting.
- Normally the Executive writes only as itself, from its own email account. Nothing goes out as you unless you set it up here.

**How to use:**

1. Click **Delegate** in the sidebar. (On a phone, open the menu with the button at the top left.)
2. Under **As you**, connect your mailbox, pick how far it goes and check how you write.
3. Under **As me**, see whether it is on or paused, and put it in training if you want to see each step first.
4. Under **Approvals**, pick the level and add any rules of your own.
5. Open **What it does for you** to see what goes out on its own today.

**What it does for you:**

- On a wide screen it sits to the right of the page. Close it with **✕**, and **What it does for you** at the top of the page brings it back; this browser remembers which. On a narrow screen, tap **What it does for you** at the top and it opens as a sheet from the bottom.
- Change a setting on the page and it updates at once. The rows that changed are marked **Just changed** for a few seconds.
- Three pills: **As you**, **Executive** and **Departments**. The number on each pill is how many things go out on their own.
- **As you** covers your own mailbox: emails you ask for in chat, inbox replies, what it sends on its own, the actions it suggests from your mail and what it has learned from your edits.
- **Executive** covers what the Executive does in its own name and meetings asked for in chat, as Approvals decides them. Only the owner sees this pill.
- **Departments** shows the Approvals level each department's work runs at and what it covers.
- Rows are grouped: **Sends on its own** (green), **Asks first** (amber), **Writes for you to send** and **Off** (grey). Each row says what it does in one line, then why, with a link to the setting.
- **Watch how: as you, and as me**, at the bottom, opens **Who writes and who sends**. Pick **As you writes**, **As you sends** or **As me** and one of its options. Three answers sit on top: who writes it, whose name is on it and who presses Send. Under them the steps appear one at a time and stay on screen, for example Dana emails you, you ask in chat, the Executive writes the draft, you tap Send. **As you sends** shows the same five emails at every level, each marked **Sent as you** or **Waits for you**. Tapping there changes no setting. **Play again** replays the steps.
- While the Executive is paused, a note at the top says nothing runs on its own, with a **Resume** link.
- Someone who is not on the People list sees "Only people on the team can see this."

**As you:**

- Who can use it: the owner. Team members can use it once the owner turns on **Let team members use it** (under **How far it goes as you**). That switch shows only when the install allows it. Anyone else sees "As you isn't available to you here."
- Each person connects their own mailbox and sets it up for themselves. What it reads in your mail, the drafts it writes and your reply cards are yours alone. The owner sees only each team member's name, how many drafts they had written and sent in the last 30 days, and whether inbox replies are on. A conversation in which it read someone's mail can be opened only by that person.
- **Your mailbox** is the first line of **How far it goes as you**: until it is connected, **How to connect it** there opens the command to run on a computer with a browser (one for Gmail and, where the install supports it, one for Outlook). Sign in as yourself, put the file it writes where the API reads it, then click **Check again**. Once connected the line reads "From your Gmail," (or Outlook) and your address. It won't connect the Executive's own address as yours.
- **How far it goes as you** (top left of the tab): under the mailbox line, pick one of three, side by side. The line under them says what the one you picked does.
  - **Off**: it never writes as you.
  - **When you ask**: ask in chat, "reply to Dana as me: yes to the 5th", and the draft waits in your Gmail or Outlook Drafts. You send it.
  - **Your inbox**: for each email that needs you, it does what the email asks where it can, writes the reply and puts it on Home. Approvals decides which go on their own.
- A **Now** line under the picker says what happens today, for example that on Balanced it sends a reply itself when it is sure and the reply leaves nothing for you to answer, and the rest wait on Home, or that in training every one waits for you.
- You can't move up from **Off** until your mailbox is connected. Moving down asks first, says what stops, and saves when you click **Move down**. Moving to **When you ask** stops inbox replies, and nothing more goes on its own as you. Moving to **Off** stops everything it writes as you and turns **Read your calendar** off.
- **In training** (its own card at the top of the second column, above **How it learns from you**, shown once it writes as you at all; the **As you** tab reads **Your inbox · In training** while it is on): a switch. On, every reply, follow-up, invite answer and suggested action waits for you, whatever Approvals says. When you send one, tick **Send to Dana on its own next time** and everything sent as you to that person goes on its own from then on, where Approvals lets it. Off, Approvals alone decides what goes on its own as you.
- **Learn from my edits** (a checkbox under it): when you change a draft before sending, tick **Do it like this next time** and it learns how you write to that person. Nothing more is sent.
- **Read your calendar**: a switch. On, it reads your own calendar when you ask about your day or week in chat, and offers your free slots when a reply needs a time. It also brings meeting invites from people you know to Home as cards (see **Meeting invites** below). The only change it makes to your calendar is answering an invite: when you tap **Accept** or **Decline**, or an accept on its own where Approvals lets it. It stays off while **How far it goes as you** is at **Off**, and while your mailbox isn't connected. If your mailbox sign-in doesn't include your calendar, the card shows a command to run once to add it. A sign-in you made before invites could be answered still reads your calendar; run the same command again to let it answer invites.
- **Suggested actions**: meeting invites and messages your mail calls for come to you as cards, and follow Approvals like its replies (see **What goes on its own as you** below).
- **How it learns from you** (the card beside **How far it goes as you**) holds everything it picked up as you, in one place: **How you write** and **How you write to each person** (from Learn from my edits). Who goes on their own, with Remove, and **Learn from my edits** are on the **In training** card above it. Each person on a list says when it was allowed or learned, how many times it has been used, and an example. **Remove** forgets it, and it asks again.
- **Sent as you on its own** (while **Your inbox** is picked): "Sent N replies on its own today". **This week** opens the list: each reply and follow-up from the last week: who it went to, the subject, and **Open in your mailbox**. An invite it accepted shows as one line, for example "Accepted Dana's Pilot review, Wed 21 Oct, 14:30", and counts toward the same daily limit.
- **How you write** is the first part of **How it learns from you** once your mailbox is connected (see below). For the owner, **Let team members use it** is a card under **How far it goes as you**. **Say it was written with AI** is on the **Approvals** tab.

**Asking in chat:**

- Ask in the web app (signed in), in a direct message to the Executive on Slack or Discord, or in a private Telegram chat: "reply to Dana as me: yes to the 5th."
- It saves a draft in your own Drafts and shows a card, "Drafted an email as you to Dana — in your Drafts". Asking in chat never sends anything by itself. In the web app the draft also appears under the reply as **Email as you**, with who it goes to, the subject and the start of the text, and a **Send** button: tapping it sends that draft from your mailbox, exactly as it was written. If you changed the draft in your mailbox first, send it from there.
- It does not write as you in a shared channel or thread, on Google Chat, from an email, from a scheduled job or in anyone else's conversation.
- If it isn't sure about something, it asks you instead of guessing.
- There is a daily limit on drafts written as one person (50 a day unless the install changes it).

**Your inbox:**

- About every five minutes it looks at new mail in your inbox. For mail that needs a personal reply from you (a question, a request, a meeting to arrange, an introduction or a follow-up), it does what the email asks where it can, writes the reply and puts it at the top of **Needs you** on Home.
- It only looks at mail that arrives after you pick **Your inbox**. It leaves out newsletters, notifications, mailing lists, automatic mail, mail you are not in To or Cc on, mail you've already answered and anything that doesn't need you. Mail you answer within ten minutes never gets a draft.
- When the email asks for something it can do, such as a document, or a spreadsheet from what's attached, it does that first and the reply delivers it; a line on the card says what it did. What it can't do or settle is listed on the card as what's left for you to decide, each with a few short answers to tap. Tap one, or **Something else…** to type your own, and it rewrites the reply with your answer. For a time, with **Read your calendar** on, it offers your next free slots. For a document, it offers one from your documents to say you'll send it (it can't attach files). **Send** waits until you've answered, or until you change the words with **Edit**. Someone you've never written to gets a short holding reply.
- Under the picker you see how it is doing (for example, that your mailbox needs connecting again) and when it last looked. Click **Check now** to look straight away.
- **Also save inbox replies in my Gmail Drafts** (or Outlook): off by default, so replies wait on their cards only. Tick it to keep each reply in your Drafts too.
- On each card on Home: **Send** asks you to confirm who it goes to, then **Send now**. In training, the card also offers **Send to Dana on its own next time**. **Edit** changes the words on the card. **Open in Gmail** opens it when it is in your Drafts. **Dismiss** removes the card.
- Limits: at most 5 drafts a check and 20 a day unless the install changes it, 2 a day per sender (1 for a stranger), and never more than 25 cards open. A card closes when the draft is sent or deleted in your mailbox, when you reply yourself, or after 7 days.

**What goes on its own as you:**

- With **Your inbox** picked, **Approvals** decides which replies, follow-ups, invites and suggested actions go from your mailbox on their own. There is no separate switch for it.
  - **Careful**: nothing goes on its own. Every reply, follow-up, invite and suggested action waits for you.
  - **Balanced**: replies and follow-ups go when it is sure and they leave nothing for you to answer, to the people the email was already with, for people you know (your team, contacts and people you've written to). A reply to anyone else waits on a card. So does a reply or follow-up about money, contracts, passwords and the like, or with a link or an amount, and an invite whose title is about one of those. Invites and suggested actions go only for your team and contacts (people on the People list for at least a week, for actions). A last look holds anything that seems to be steering it.
  - **Hands-off**: the same, and replies also go to people you don't know yet, invites for people you've written to, and suggested actions for anyone, new contacts included.
- **In training** holds all of it until you allow each person, whatever the level.
- Sending on its own needs signed sign-ins on the server. Without them everything waits on cards.
- Whatever the level, it never writes to anyone the email didn't go to, never sends twice in a row in a conversation, never declines a meeting on its own, and a reply that names the Executive, or leaves you something to answer, waits for you on Home.
- **Say it was written with AI** (on the **Approvals** tab, when the install adds an AI line): two switches, for the drafts you send and for the replies it sends on its own. Turning one off asks you to confirm.
- Limits: 20 replies sent on its own a day unless the install changes it, and one a conversation a day. Suggested actions: up to 10 a day. Past the limit, they wait on cards.

**Meeting invites (with Read your calendar on):**

- An invite from someone you know (your team, a contact, or someone you've written to) becomes a card in **Needs you** on Home: the meeting, when it is, who invited you and anything on your calendar it clashes with. Only the busy times are shown, never what the other meetings are.
- **Accept** or **Decline** answers it in your own calendar, and your calendar lets them know. **Dismiss** removes the card without answering. In training, **Accept** also offers **Accept from Dana on its own next time**: their invites with no clash, and everything else sent as you to them, go on their own from then on.
- Invites from people you don't know, from an address your mail service couldn't confirm, meetings that aren't on your calendar, ones you've already answered and ones that have started are left alone, as before.
- If your sign-in can read your calendar but not answer invites, the card says so and shows the command to connect again under **Read your calendar**. Until then, answer it in your calendar.
- A card closes by itself once the meeting starts, or after 7 days.

**How you write (in How it learns from you, once your mailbox is connected):**

- Shows your style as a few sentences, with where it came from ("Learned from N of your sent emails", or "Set by you") and whether it is locked.
- **Describe it in your own words**: write how you write, the way you'd tell a new assistant (up to 2,000 characters). Buttons add common phrases, such as "Short and to the point" or "No emojis". Click **Write my style**; it shows the new style with new lines marked **New** and a sample reply. Click **Save** to keep it or **Change it** to edit your words. Nothing changes until you save.
- **Learn from my sent mail** (or **Learn again from my sent mail**): reads your recent sent emails once and describes how you write. It needs your mailbox connected and is hidden while the style is locked.
- **Fine-tune details** opens the fields: **Length** (short, medium, long), **Tone** (casual, neutral, formal), a **Greeting** **To your team**, **To your contacts** and **To anyone else** ({first} becomes their first name), **Sign-off**, **Habits** and **Never** (one per line), your **Signature** and **Examples of your writing**.
- **Save changes** saves the fields. **Lock** stops it being relearned from your mail (you can still edit it); **Unlock** undoes that. **Reset** starts over. **Remove examples** drops the examples.
- **Signature**: with Gmail, your signature is added to every draft. **Refresh from Gmail** picks up a change you made in Gmail, **Don't add my signature** stops adding it, and **Add my Gmail signature** brings it back. Outlook doesn't share signatures with apps, so Outlook drafts end with your sign-off.

**As me:**

- In its own name, without being asked. Every day before your brief it looks over Home, open tasks, alerts and what people said, and acts: it follows up with people, books or moves meetings, starts workflows, assigns tasks and makes changes in your connected apps. People can see it's the Executive.
- This tab holds its settings. What it did, what it left for you and what it is watching are on **Home** (**Done for you**, **Needs you** and **Watching next**). The first card says how many things it did today and how many it left for you, with **Open Home**.
- **Standing jobs** (the owner only): things you asked it to keep doing, such as "Keep the dealer onboarding moving". Each shows since when and what it did for it this week (follow-ups, meetings booked, other steps), with **Stop**. Type one in **Give me a standing job…** and press Enter, or say it in chat ("keep chasing overdue tasks every morning"). Every time it looks it works the jobs where there is something to do. Each step still goes through Approvals, your rules and In training, the same as anything else it does.
- **When I look**: every day before your brief, and when any of these happen: new mail, a chat message, a goal slips (on track to at risk, or worse), a workflow fails, a meeting on your calendar ends, a task goes overdue. A burst of these is one look, a few minutes later, and it looks at most every half hour.
- **Pause everything**: the same switch as **Pause everything** on **Settings → Your Executive**. Paused, the Executive only answers when asked: no briefs, nudges, monitoring or work in its own name. Anything you tap **Send** or **Approve** on still goes. A **Now** line under it says what Approvals lets it do today.
- **In training** (the owner only): a switch. On, everything it would do in its own name comes to you as a card on Home first, whatever Approvals says. The card says what it would have done. Approve it and it does that once; tick **Do this on its own next time** and it does that for the same person or thing without asking from then on, where Approvals lets it. Off, Approvals alone decides what waits for your yes.
- **What it's learned** (on the In training card): what you have allowed, each with when, how many times it has been done since, and an example. **Remove** forgets it, and it asks again. What you have approved three times unchanged is offered under **Could go on its own** on the **Approvals** tab, and on its next card on Home.
- A meeting you ask for in chat books straight away. A teammate's waits for approval unless Approvals is on Hands-off.
- Anyone who is not the owner sees the Pause everything card, and that only the account owner can put the Executive in training or allow what it does on its own.

**Approvals:**

- **Approvals** is one setting for both sides, the owner's alone. Everyone else sees the level it is on. It is the same on every channel: the app, email and every chat app. Pick **Careful**, **Balanced** (the starting choice) or **Hands-off**; it saves when you pick. **Settings → Your Executive** shows the level and links here. To change it from any page, use **Approvals** at the bottom of the sidebar: it shows the current level, clicking it opens the three levels to pick from, and **More on Delegate** at its foot comes here.
- **Approvals** shows **Careful**, **Balanced** (recommended) and **Hands-off** side by side, with a line on the one you picked. **What each level means** under it opens the three levels, the current one marked:
  - **Careful**. As you: nothing goes on its own. As me: every action waits for your yes.
  - **Balanced**. As you: replies and follow-ups go when it's sure, to the people the email was already with; invites and suggested actions go for your team and contacts. As me: your team and contacts go. Someone new, money, contracts, people decisions, deleting or sharing, and sends to more than five people wait.
  - **Hands-off**. As you: the same, and replies to people you don't know yet, invites from people you've written to and suggested actions for anyone go too. As me: everything goes. Only your rules still wait.
- In training, on either side, holds everything for you first, whatever the level.
- Under the level, a line says what it did in the last 7 days, As you and As me together, for you: for example **Last 7 days: 23 went on their own, 6 waited for you**, then how many of those you approved and declined and the most common reason they waited. **See what waited** opens the list, each with when, why it waited and what you did. The line is hidden while both counts are 0.
- **Could go on its own** (between the level and Your rules) lists what you approved three times without changing it in the last 30 days, As you and As me together: for As you, replies to one person while As you is in training; for As me (the owner only), something it did in training. Each says **As you** or **As me**, how many times and when last. **Let it go** lets it go on its own from then on, where Approvals lets it, exactly as ticking **on its own next time** on its card would, and it joins **What it's learned**. **Keep asking** stops offering it until you approve it unchanged three more times. The same offer shows on its next card on Home. The card is hidden when there is nothing to offer. Careful, Your rules and In training still decide in the same order.
- **Your rules** (the owner only) change what the level decides, for both As you and As me. With none, the level alone decides. Each rule is about an amount, a person, a company (an email domain) or words, and is one of two kinds:
  - **Waits** (Always wait for me): anything that matches waits for your yes, on every level. An amount rule waits for that amount or more.
  - **Goes** (Goes on its own): anything it covers goes without asking where Balanced would ask first, for example **Amounts under 500** for money. Each covers only its own part: an amount rule the money, when every amount is under the limit and the amount is in what it sends; a person or company rule anything that goes only to that person or to people at that company. A words rule can only wait, since what an email says can end up in what it sends. A reply as you that carries a link or a password still waits below Hands-off. A delete or share, someone who isn't in People asking by email, and something it read trying to give it orders still wait.
  - The order: **Careful** holds everything; a Waits rule wins over a Goes rule; a Goes rule lets it through, or else the level decides; **In training** is the last check, so while it is on nothing goes out on its own, rules included, except what you ticked to do on its own next time.
  - Once you have rules, a line under the level says what they change, for example **Your rules change this: 2 go on their own, 2 always wait.** **See rules** jumps to the list. Each rule shows **Waits** or **Goes**; **Remove** takes it off. **Add a rule** opens the form: pick **Always wait for me** or **Goes on its own**, what it's about, the value, then **Add rule** (or **Cancel**). Adding a Goes rule needs signed sign-ins on a server, like removing one.
  - A card held by a rule says so.
- **Say it was written with AI** (under Your rules, when the install adds an AI line): one card for the line it adds to what goes out. The **As you** row has your own two switches, for the drafts you send and for the replies it sends on its own as you.
- Pause, what it always does without asking, and the voice it answers in are under **Settings → Your Executive**.

**Approve cards in your chat app:**

- A held action, reply or invite reaches you in Telegram, Slack or Discord too, when the Executive is connected there. The card has **Approve** (or **Send**, **Accept**) and **Skip**, and in training a third button, for example **Send + on its own next time**, which does it once and allows it from then on, the same as the tick in the app.

**Example prompts:**

- "Reply to Dana as me: yes to the 5th, and ask her to send the deck first."
- "Write to the Acme team as me and push our call to Thursday."
- "What's on my calendar tomorrow?" (with **Read your calendar** on)
